item.text: {"classifications":[{"segment_id":"1","code":3,"rationale":"The President presently establishes the medal and makes qualifying Armed Forces members eligible for it; those legal consequences occur in the segment itself, while the Secretary’s later design approval is ministerial implementation.","evidence":"Members of the Armed Forces of the United States (including Reserve components) who perform outstanding volunteer service to the civilian community of a sustained, direct, and consequential nature are eligible for the medal."},{"segment_id":"2","code":4,"rationale":"The segment inseparably combines a mandate that the Secretary later prescribe regulations producing a specified order of precedence with present presidential rules limiting awards and authorizing posthumous awards; these are materially different Code 2 and Code 3 postures.","evidence":"The regulations shall place the Military Outstanding Volunteer Service Medal in order of precedence immediately after the Humanitarian Service Medal."}]}
